about: Every image asset Eldmoor wants (#177). npm run art:daily (scripts/art/daily.mjs) generates the missing ones in priority order on the owner's private ZeroGPU Space (#703: provider space, daily GPU quota, $0; --provider router uses Hugging Face Inference Providers, billed, up to the day's share of the monthly credits) until the GPU quota is used, into assets/incoming/<date>/ for review; npm run art:accept moves reviewed ones into assets/ and assets/index.json. Each asset has a procedural fallback (its hook); a missing file never breaks a world. Data only: no game code reads prompts.

schema.id: '<kind>:<name>', unique; name is lower-case letters, digits and '-'. The file is assets/<kind>/<name>.png.
schema.kind: tile | autotile | building | landmark | sprite | portrait | prop | icon (must equal the id's prefix)
schema.priority: a priorities[].n: the daily run makes lower numbers first, then manifest order
schema.sizes: {"32": [w, h], "64": [w, h]}: pixels after post-processing at each tier (src/render/tile.js TIERS); the renderer uses the tier of its TILE. One entry, one prompt and one seed for every tier, so a 64 set is a regeneration pass, not new design
schema.frames: sprite sheets only: {cols, rows}: frame columns (stand, step, other step) and rows (facing down, left, right, up); every tier's size splits into them. Post-processing (scripts/art/post-sheet.mjs) finds the model's cols x rows figures, scales them alike and sets each on its frame's floor; a sheet without them, or a hero sheet (palette from SPRITE.key) whose tabard is missing in most frames, is rejected and its raw image kept
schema.model: optional key of 'models'; default: pinnedModel, else the first candidate that answers (recorded in assets/queue.json)
schema.prompt: what to draw; the model's trigger word and the top-level 'style' are added around it
schema.seed: integer, fixed so a regeneration is reproducible where the provider honours seeds (alternates and rejected redraws add an offset)
schema.palette: {from: [paths into src/render/palette.js exports, e.g. 'BIOME.meadow'], extra: ['#rrggbb', ...]}: the only colours the asset may use
schema.post: {fit: 'crop' (tiles: a seamless window of the model image at its own pixel scale) | 'scale' (shrink the subject), grid?: block size hint in px (default the model's grid, else 8), tone: bool (match the palette's tones, default true), dither: RGB amplitude of a 4x4 ordered dither (0 = none), minPalette: widen a short palette with shades to this many colours (6), minColors: an output with fewer colours is rejected as flat (default 4 for tiles, 2 otherwise), downscale: 'mode'|'mean' (scale fit), transparent: bool, bgTolerance: number, outline: bool, outlineColor?: '#rrggbb', fundamental: false keeps the first grid period found instead of the real pixel size under it (tile:ash-rock, accepted that way), shape: false skips the transition piece check of autotiles; sprite sheets: tone is off unless true, outline on unless false, keyFrames (frames that must show the faction key, default half), keyMin (key pixels that count as showing it, 3)}
schema.init: 'procedural': made image to image from the game's own art (#763, scripts/art/init.mjs): the Space gets it as the init image and the output keeps its silhouette (false: text only). Usually from kindInit
schema.strength: how far the model may go from the init image, .1 to .9 (diffusers img2img strength; low keeps view, silhouette, footprint and palette). Usually from kindInit
schema.kindInit: {kind: {init, strength}}: entries of those kinds (building, landmark, sprite) take these unless they set their own
schema.kindModel: {on, model, kinds: [kind], about}: with on, entries of those kinds without their own 'model' use this model (a trial switch, #763)
schema.kindStyle: optional {kind: style}: replaces 'style' in the prompts of that kind (buildings and landmarks are not seamless ground)
schema.hook: {module: renderer file, export: the object in it that names this id with its procedural fallback, fallback: words}

priorities.name: terrain tileset (slice 2): base tiles per biome, road, water, transition edges, corners and inner corners, tree and rock variants
portrait library (slice 5): about 40 faces per people x class, picked by hash at founding

allowance.source: https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers/pricing (read 2026-11-03): free accounts get no Inference Providers credits, PRO $2.00 a month, extra use is pay-as-you-go. daily.mjs spends at most monthlyUsd / days-in-month a day and stops for the month at monthlyUsd. carry: a day that made nothing adds its share to the next days of the month (the loop, art:loop). These apply to --provider router only (#703).

zeroGpu.source: https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/spaces-zerogpu (read 2026-11-03): PRO accounts get 40 minutes of ZeroGPU a day, reset 24 hours after the first use; past it, use is billed to pre-paid credits ($1 per 10 minutes) when the token allows it. The default provider (#703, the owner's private Space) counts GPU seconds in that window (assets/queue.json gpu) and stops at stopAtMinutes (ART_GPU_MINUTES overrides) or at the Space's quota refusal, so it never runs into overage.

kindModel.about: #763: pixel-xl ignores view instructions (front elevations instead of the game's top-down three-quarter view); the FLUX pixel LoRA follows them better. With on: true every entry of these kinds that names no model of its own is made with this model (scripts/art/lib.mjs loadManifest). Before turning it on for the ZeroGPU Space: the Space must load FLUX.1-dev with this LoRA (scripts/art/space/app.py loads SDXL only today) and the model needs space: tsc862/eldmoor-art; until then the Space run says no model is on the Space, and --provider router makes them on the billed router (about $0.035 an image).

kindInit.about: #763, owner decision 2026-11-03: buildings, landmarks and sprites are made image to image from the procedural art, so the game's view, silhouette, footprint, frame grid and palette are kept and the model adds texture and character only. On the Space only (the img2img API); tiles, props, portraits and backdrops stay text only. Strength from the img2img guide (diffusers, read 2026-11-03): low stays close to the init; sprites lowest, because their frames and tabard must survive.

tiers.about: Generation settings per tier (src/render/tile.js TILE is the tier the renderer draws; art:daily and art:gen take --tier, default TILE). From the owner's three-tier comparison on 2026-11-03 (pixel-xl, same prompt and seed, LoRA scale 1.0 / 0.55 / 0.2, reduced to 128 / 256 / 512 px): the 32 tier sits near LoRA scale 0.55 with the model's pixel grid read as 4 px, the 64 tier near 0.2 with grid 2. A model's own tiers{} overrides these. minPalette widens each asset's palette with shades (src/render/palette.js TIER_SHADES).

style: top-down 2d game tile seen from directly above, 16-bit era JRPG overworld, crisp pixels, flat colours, no perspective, seamless

kindStyle.building: a 16-bit era JRPG overworld town piece in the look of the game's own houses (#763): light from the top left, crisp pixels, a few flat colours, a thick dark outline
kindStyle.landmark: a set piece of a 16-bit era JRPG overworld seen from directly above, light from the top left, crisp pixels, flat colours
kindStyle.sprite: a 16-bit era JRPG character sprite sheet, every figure the same size in a neat grid with clear empty space between them, light from the top left, crisp pixels, flat colours, plain white background

negativeStyle: text, watermark, signature, border, frame, photo, realistic, 3d render, blurry, gradient, perspective, isometric, horizon, sky

pixel-xl.why: Most-liked pixel-art model on the Hub (666 likes), an SDXL LoRA live on fal-ai through Inference Providers; its card advises downscaling by 8, which post-processing does.
pixel-xl.firstRun: 2026-11-03: answered 5 of 5 (estimate $0.01 an image; confirm on https://huggingface.co/settings/billing). Its tiles came out flat under the first post-processing; post-texture.mjs fixes that.

pixel-redmond.why: Second SDXL pixel-art LoRA on the same fal-ai route; a different look if the first is refused.

ume-flux.why: FLUX.1-dev pixel-art LoRA (MIT), live on fal-ai; better prompt following, dearer per image.

z-turbo.why: Z-Image-Turbo pixel-art LoRA (Apache-2.0), live on fal-ai; 8 steps, cheap.

flux-schnell.why: Last resort: a base model (no pixel LoRA) on fal-ai; the post-processing still forces the pixel grid and palette.

costNote: costPerImage values are estimates of what a call draws from the account's Inference Providers credits, not quoted prices. Credits are monthly ($2.00 on PRO, none on a free account); past them use is pay-as-you-go if the account has a payment method, so daily.mjs stops at its own budget (allowance) before relying on a 402.
